s1.syndrome_frame: Bilateral ocular inflammation with recent onset of blurred vision and ocular irritation, accompanied by systemic symptoms such as fever and arthralgia, and neurological complications
salient_findings: Stromal immune ring formation with underlying keratic precipitates
Positive for Chikungunya virus with weak viral load
key_facts: Patient is a teenage girl from Saint-Martin
Presented with bilateral blurred vision and ocular irritation
Experienced fever and severe arthralgia one month earlier
Neurological complications are present
Recently acquired periorbital hyperpigmentation
Ocular history is negative for trauma and previous inflammation
Primary HIV infection, tuberculosis, sarcoidosis, and syphilis have been ruled out
Best-corrected visual acuity is 20/20 OU
Slitlamp biomicroscopy revealed bilateral punctate superficial keratitis and stromal immune ring formation
Aqueous tap PCR results are positive for Chikungunya virus with weak viral load
IgM CHIKV serologic test is positive

shortlist.label: uveitis
shortlist.why_kept: bilateral ocular inflammation and positive Chikungunya virus PCR results

shortlist.label: keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: bilateral punctate superficial keratitis and stromal immune ring formation

shortlist.label: choroiditis
shortlist.why_kept: systemic symptoms such as fever and arthralgia, and neurological complications

shortlist.label: vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: recent onset of blurred vision and ocular irritation, accompanied by systemic symptoms

shortlist.label: neurotrophic keratitis
shortlist.why_kept: bilateral ocular inflammation and recent acquisition of periorbital hyperpigmentation

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of bilateral blurred vision, ocular irritation, and slitlamp biomicroscopy findings of bilateral punctate superficial keratitis and stromal immune ring formation are consistent with keratitis, and the aqueous tap PCR results positive for Chikungunya virus with weak viral load support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: uveitis
rejected.why: While the patient has some signs of inflammation, the primary findings are localized to the cornea, making uveitis less likely.

rejected.label: choroiditis
rejected.why: The normal fundus examination makes choroiditis unlikely.

rejected.label: vasculitis
rejected.why: There is no clear evidence of vasculitis, such as retinal or conjunctival vessel inflammation.

rejected.label: neurotrophic keratitis
rejected.why: The patient's corneal findings are not consistent with neurotrophic keratitis, which typically presents with a more severe epithelial defect and stromal thinning.
